question: What owns table topology, cell coordinates, selection, clipboard and layout?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles final-pass reassessment; method-level public API inventory; private planner/canonical transaction ownership comparison
trigger: After the initial table review was recorded, the user requested a last pass to make sure nothing material was missed. This authorizes a fresh assessment and linked review record, not product execution or publication.
requirements: Reassess the initial table verdict from first principles rather than merely proofreading it.
Audit the method-level public surface, including production callers, DOM types and leaked compiler or cache protocols.
Distinguish duplicate change authority from a private pure plan that may earn its place through detached simulation, deterministic diagnostics and atomic rejection.
Preserve the initial reproduced correctness findings and all stated proof limits unless fresh evidence defeats them.
Leave one corrected durable target and one next owner without changing product code.
evidenceReuse: The source manifest is unchanged since 2026-09-16-table-canonical-edits, so its fresh package partitions and source-bound failure probe remain valid evidence and were not rerun. This pass re-read BaseTablePlugin, TablePlugin, table types, mutation/paste interpreters and Plite transaction-spec construction. A production-consumer search added method-level API evidence. No browser, stress run or external discovery was added.
summary: Pursue Task design/plan. The initial correctness verdict stands, but this record supersedes its ordering of the hard cut. The strongest proven deletion is the accidental public protocol: DOM-bound writeSelection on the headless table API, unused convenience/navigation exports, public grid/context/compiler metrics, unused transfer provenance and the orphan selected-cell drag path. TableOperation is a private deterministic plan used for detached repair, replay and atomic diagnostics; replacing it with canonical transaction specs is a candidate, not an accepted cut, until a complete-operation comparison proves those jobs survive with less authority and complexity. The durable target is one canonical committed change owner, one private table geometry/policy owner, complete-slice preservation and explicit root-aware targets.
alternatives: Keep/configure still loses: reproduced rich-content loss, complete-slice truncation, ignored explicit targets, fabricated coordinates and unenforced merge policy are contract failures.

Change existing APIs: use one explicit root-aware target contract across structural commands, return honest absence or rejection, make construction schema-valid and expose a small domain selection result instead of grid/compiler internals.

Delete the proven accidental surface: make table clipboard serialization private to the DOM/React adapter; remove or privatize unconsumed getCellChildren, isRectangular, getCellIndicesByKey, row/linear navigation aliases and presentation-state aliases unless a real external job is demonstrated.

Retain public presentation reads only where copied renderers genuinely need them, such as resolved column widths, cell layout and border state; redesign them around domain answers rather than compiler inputs.
Delete unused paste-source provenance and the orphan selected-cell drag capture/MIME/drop protocol. Keep real row drag-and-drop, generic clipboard behavior and mounted resize lifecycle.

Keep TableOperation private for the design comparison. Candidate A retains a domain plan but compiles it once to a canonical TransactionSpec; candidate B authors a canonical candidate transaction directly; candidate C returns transformed detached tables. Accept only the smallest candidate that preserves deterministic diagnostics, detached source repair, atomic rejection, named roots, history and measured end-to-end cost.

Keep table geometry and policy in Plate, canonical changes and complete-slice fitting in Plite, mounted gestures and DOM paint in React, and copied visual controls in the registry UI. Do not add a table controller, public grid store or generic table package.

Keep table, row and cell descriptors, the single header property, automatic dependencies and the September resize split; those nouns still have independent grammar, codec, renderer or interaction jobs.
proofLimits: Assessment only; no product edits, declaration/type closure, browser/device run, import stress, authored-view runtime reproduction or candidate benchmark. Reused evidence from the immediately preceding source-identical record: 236 core table tests and 48 React table tests passed, and its source-bound probe reproduced merge media loss, mixed-slice sibling loss, target violations and the merge-policy contradiction. The production-caller inventory is bounded to repository source and excludes tests, slow fixtures, generated public artifacts and documentation. It supports privatization candidates, not a claim that downstream npm users do not call those APIs. TableOperation replacement remains explicitly unaccepted until complete fitting/publication, rollback, rich and named-root content, history, authored views and scale are compared.
